sections.content: In a full story the three past tenses work together. The *imperfecto* sets the scene, the *indefinido* moves the action on, and the *pluscuamperfecto* reaches back to what had already happened. Connectors hold it all together.

sections.title: One story, three past tenses
rows: Don Quijote caminaba por La Mancha.
De niño había leído muchas historias de caballeros.
Por eso creyó que eran gigantes.

items.spanish: Mientras caminaban por el campo, Don Quijote vio unos molinos.
items.english: While they were walking through the countryside, Don Quijote saw some windmills.

items.spanish: Sancho intentó explicarle la verdad; sin embargo, él no lo escuchó.
items.english: Sancho tried to explain the truth to him; however, he didn't listen.

items.spanish: Antes de llegar, ya había decidido que sería una gran batalla.
items.english: Before arriving, he had already decided it would be a great battle.
In the end, they returned to the road.

sections.content: While you read, sort each verb: is it the scene, an event, or something earlier? When you retell a story, keep that order of ideas and pick the tense that matches each role.
